definition: The weighted average gap between confidence and accuracy across confidence bins, and across 4 sources the standard calibration metric in this archive. Its reported values place the scale: on three medical benchmarks the best system reaches 0.202, 0.115 and 0.290 while baselines run to 0.587, so the range in practice is wide and no archived model is close to calibrated on hard sets. The archive's methodological caution about it is specific and applies to one of its own sources: a training objective that optimises mean answer-token probability and an error computed by binning the same quantity are not independent measurements, so a fall in the metric is partly a check that optimisation succeeded. A second caution is structural -- binning makes the number sensitive to the bin count and to the confidence distribution, so a comparison is only meaningful under a fixed protocol, which several sources state and none varies.

evidence.note: Replaces PPO's scalar mean-squared-error critic head with a categorical predictor over a discretized value support trained by cross-entropy against Gaussian-smoothed targets, decodes it back to a scalar for an unchanged GAE update, and shows the resulting critic is better calibrated and produces near-symmetric advantages where the MSE critic penalizes failures two-to-three times harder than it rewards successes.
evidence.title: Start Classifying: Categorical Critics for LLM Reinforcement Learning

evidence.note: Independently reproduces two published reliability methods and stress-tests them across models and domains their authors never tried, finding one reproduces exactly but loses significance everywhere new, and the other rests on a decodable logic direction that a same-norm random direction matches exactly under steering.
evidence.title: Reproducing and Stress-Testing Two Approaches to LLM Reasoning Reliability: Test-Time Probability Aggregation and Logic-Representation Editing

evidence.note: Adds a correctness-conditioned confidence term to the GRPO reward for medical visual question answering -- rewarding answer-token confidence when the answer is right and penalising it when wrong -- on top of an SFT cold start built from answer-conditioned reasoning traces filtered by a verifier.
evidence.title: CARE: Confidence-Aware Reasoning for Reliable Medical VQA

evidence.note: Finds diffusion language models are badly miscalibrated on math reasoning yet rank correct from incorrect far better than autoregressive baselines, because their confidence tracks structural consistency rather than correctness.
evidence.title: The Confidence Paradox: Unveiling the Latent Discriminative Power of Diffusion Large Language Models in Mathematical Reasoning

name: expected calibration error
